# ui

Namespace-scope declarations of `ui` from the core headers.

## Enumerations

### Handling

```cpp
enum class Handling : std::uint8_t
```

Header: `winui/core/Callback.hpp`.

What a handler asked to act returns: whether it dealt with the event, so it goes no further. Written as the constants [ui::Handled](#handled) and [ui::NotHandled](#nothandled). A handler that returns nothing gets its event's default: handled where the handler is the target asked to act (a shortcut, a context-menu request), not handled where it watches events pass by ([`Window::on_key_preview`](../tree/window.md#on_key_preview)).

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Handled` | Dealt with; the event goes no further. |
| `NotHandled` | Not this handler's; the event goes on. |

### Decision

```cpp
enum class Decision : std::uint8_t
```

Header: `winui/core/Callback.hpp`.

What a handler asked before something happens returns: let it go ahead, or stop it (a window closing, an edit starting or being committed, a sort). Written as the constants [ui::Proceed](#proceed) and [ui::Cancel](#cancel). A handler that returns nothing lets it proceed.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Proceed` | Go ahead. |
| `Cancel` | Stop it; nothing changes. |

### DirtyFlags

```cpp
enum class DirtyFlags : std::uint8_t
```

Header: `winui/core/DirtyFlags.hpp`.

Bitmask of what about an [Element](../tree/element.md) is out of date and must be redone at the next layout pass.

Setters mark flags on their element and the bits bubble to every ancestor, so a host can ask the root whether anything below it changed. On the element itself `Measure` and `Arrange` also say its own last measure or arrange is out of date. On an ancestor they only say something below needs it. Combine with `|`, test with `&` or [any()](#any), clear with `&= ~flags`. Read back through [Element::is_dirty()](../tree/element.md#is_dirty) / [Element::dirty_flags()](../tree/element.md#dirty_flags); [Window::layout()](../tree/window.md#layout) clears them.

Example: 
```cpp
// In a custom control, each setter marks what its change invalidates.
class TagControl : public ui::Element
{
public:
    void set_label(std::string label)
    {
        if (label_ != label)
        {
            label_ = std::move(label);
            mark_dirty(ui::DirtyFlags::Layout | ui::DirtyFlags::Visual); // new size and new look
        }
    }

    void set_highlighted(bool highlighted)
    {
        if (highlighted_ != highlighted)
        {
            highlighted_ = highlighted;
            mark_dirty(ui::DirtyFlags::Visual); // same size and place, only a redraw
        }
    }

private:
    std::string label_;
    bool        highlighted_ = false;
};

// Outside the element: has anything below the panel changed size since the last layout pass?
bool needs_measure(const ui::Element& panel)
{
    return panel.is_dirty(ui::DirtyFlags::Measure); // measured again at the next layout
}
```

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `None` | Up to date. |
| `Measure` | The desired size must be recomputed, and so the arrangement too. |
| `Visual` | Appearance changed (color, focus ring, scroll offset, ...); size and place unaffected. |
| `Arrange` | The place of the element or its children changed, its desired size did not. |
| `Layout` | Measure and arrange: what a size-affecting setter marks. |
| `All` | Every flag; the default mask of the queries. |

### CursorShape

Header: `winui/core/Input.hpp`.

### Key

```cpp

```

Header: `winui/core/Input.hpp`.

The keys a control or a shortcut reads: navigation and editing keys, letters, digits, function keys and the keypad operators. Any other key arrives as Unknown.

Example: 
```cpp
const ui::KeyCombo save = ui::Ctrl + ui::Key::S; // save.text() is "Ctrl+S"

// In an element of your own:
class FileListControl : public ui::Element
{
protected:
    bool key_override(const ui::KeyEvent& e) override
    {
        if (e.action == ui::KeyAction::Down && e.key == ui::Key::Delete)
        {
            remove_selected();
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }

private:
    void remove_selected();
};
```

### RoundingAlgorithm

```cpp
enum class RoundingAlgorithm
```

Header: `winui/core/NumberFormat.hpp`.

How [IncrementNumberRounder](increment-number-rounder.md) picks between the two neighboring multiples of its increment.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `RoundDown` | toward negative infinity |
| `RoundUp` | toward positive infinity |
| `RoundTowardsZero` | truncate: -2.7 becomes -2 |
| `RoundAwayFromZero` | away from zero: -2.2 becomes -3 |
| `RoundHalfDown` | nearest; a tie toward negative infinity |
| `RoundHalfUp` | nearest; a tie toward positive infinity |
| `RoundHalfTowardsZero` | nearest; a tie toward zero |
| `RoundHalfAwayFromZero` | nearest; a tie away from zero (school rounding) |
| `RoundHalfToEven` | nearest; a tie to the even multiple (banker's rounding): 2.5 becomes 2 |
| `RoundHalfToOdd` | nearest; a tie to the odd multiple: 2.5 becomes 3 |

## Aliases

### Action

```cpp
using ui::Action = Callback<void()>
```

Header: `winui/core/Callback.hpp`.

The most common shape, [`Callback<void()>`](callback.md), named because it reads better in a spec field: `.on_click = [&] { save(); }`.

### Duration

```cpp
using ui::Duration = std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>
```

Header: `winui/core/Duration.hpp`.

A length of time: every delay, duration, interval and elapsed time in the API. Milliseconds with a fractional part, so `std::chrono_literals` write it (`800ms`, `0.3s`, `2s`) and a frame step of 16.7 ms keeps its fraction. A bare number does not convert, so a value always says its unit.

Example: 
```cpp
using namespace std::chrono_literals;

ui::Property<std::string> hint{"Saved"};
window.set_content(ui::ToolTip{
    .delay   = 400ms,
    .anchor  = ui::Button{ .text = "Refresh" },
    .content = ui::Text{ .text = "Reload the list" },
});
ui::Subscription hide_hint = window.after(2s, [&] { hint = ""; });
```

### NativeHandle

```cpp
using ui::NativeHandle = HWND__*
```

Header: `winui/core/NativeHandle.hpp`.

The operating system's own handle of a window or a hosted control, for the calls libwinui does not wrap. On Windows it is the same type as `HWND`, declared here without `<windows.h>`, so a real HWND passes in and out unchanged; elsewhere it is an opaque pointer. Null while the window does not exist.

Example:

```cpp
if (const ui::NativeHandle hwnd = window.native_handle())
{
    FlashWindow(hwnd, TRUE); // any Win32 call libwinui doesn't wrap
}
```

## Functions

### lerp

```cpp
Color lerp(const Color& a, const Color& b, float t)
```

Header: `winui/core/Color.hpp`.

Channel-wise linear interpolation from `a` (t = 0) to `b` (t = 1), alpha included. `t` is clamped to [0, 1]. Interpolates the stored sRGB values directly, not in linear light.

### command_line

```cpp
std::vector<std::string> command_line()
```

Header: `winui/core/CommandLine.hpp`.

Every argument, UTF-8 encoded, the program itself first (argv[0]'s place), so an app that wants only what the user passed starts at index 1. A path argument goes through [path_from_utf8()](#path_from_utf8) (core/Utf8Path.hpp), not std::filesystem::path's own std::string constructor. Re-reads the process command line on every call; empty only where no source exists.

Example: 
```cpp
int main()
{
    const std::vector<std::string> args = ui::command_line();
    const std::filesystem::path folder =
        args.size() > 1 ? ui::path_from_utf8(args[1]) : std::filesystem::current_path();
    // ... open `folder` ...
    return 0;
}
```

### round_significant

```cpp
double round_significant(double value, int digits)
```

Header: `winui/core/NumberFormat.hpp`.

`value` rounded to `digits` significant digits. [NumberBox](../controls/number-box.md#uinumberbox) rounds its display to 10, which hides the digits floating-point arithmetic leaves behind (0.1 + 0.2 shows as 0.3). `digits` counts significant digits, not fraction digits. NaN and the infinities pass through.

### evaluate_expression

```cpp
std::optional<double> evaluate_expression(std::string_view expression, const DecimalFormatter& parser)
```

Header: `winui/core/NumberFormat.hpp`.

Evaluates an arithmetic expression of numbers, `+ - * / ^`, parentheses and spaces. Numbers are read with `parser`, so in its locale: "1,5 + 2" is 3.5 where the decimal separator is ",". `^` binds tighter than `* /`, which bind tighter than `+ -`, and each is left-associative. A division by zero is NaN, and anything malformed is nullopt.

### bind

```cpp
template <typename T>
Binding<std::vector<T>> bind(ObservableVector<T>& source)
```

Header: `winui/core/ObservableVector.hpp`.

[Binding](binding.md) of a collection to an `.items` field: the field follows every insert, removal, replacement and move, row by row. [ui::ForEach](../controls/for-each.md#uiforeach) then passes each item to `.item` as `T&`.

A field that reads the collection in place ([ui::ForEach](../controls/for-each.md#uiforeach), the views) never copies it. On a field that only takes a whole vector (a shape's `.points`), the binding delivers a copy of the collection when the field is built and on every change, which needs a copyable item type.

### bind

```cpp
template <typename T>
Binding<std::vector<T>> bind(const ObservableVector<T>& source)
    requires std::copy_constructible<T>
```

Header: `winui/core/ObservableVector.hpp`.

[Binding](binding.md) of a collection the caller may only read. The field gets a copy of the whole collection when it is built and again after every change, as from a [`Property<std::vector<T>>`](property.md); it never writes to the collection, so a view built from it does not reorder it by drag.

Header: `winui/core/ObservableVector.hpp`.

One-way binding of a list made from one [Property](property.md) of each item: the values of `member` in collection order. It follows both the collection (an item added, removed or moved) and each item's [Property](property.md), so a list of choices whose texts the user edits stays a plain `std::vector` for a control's `.items`.

Example: 
```cpp
struct Choice
{
    ui::Property<std::string> text;
};
ui::ObservableVector<Choice> choices;
choices.emplace_back().text = "Small";
window.set_content(ui::ComboBox{.items = ui::bind_each(choices, &Choice::text)});
choices.emplace_back().text = "Large"; // the drop-down lists both
choices[0].text             = "Tiny";  // and follows the edit
```

### bind_each

```cpp
template <typename T, typename U>
Binding<std::vector<U>> bind_each(const ObservableVector<T>&& items, Property<U> T::* member) = delete
```

Header: `winui/core/ObservableVector.hpp`.

Deleted: the binding keeps a reference to the collection, so a temporary cannot be bound.

### item_count

```cpp
template <typename T, typename K>
ItemCount item_count(const Property<std::vector<T>>& source, K key)
    requires std::constructible_from<ItemKey<T>, K> && std::copy_constructible<K>
```

Header: `winui/core/ObservableVector.hpp`.

The size of the vector in `source`, kept current, with each change of the property reported as what happened to the items: what an index-based collection spec's [`.item_count`](#item_count) takes to follow a [`ui::Property<std::vector<T>>`](property.md) the app assigns as a whole. The typed views ([ui::ListView](../controls/list-view.md#uilistview), [ui::TileView](../controls/tile-view.md#uitileview), [ui::TableView](../controls/table-view.md#uitableview)) do the same from `.items` and `.key`.

`key` says which item is which (a member pointer or a callable, see [ui::ItemKey](item-key.md)). An item whose key is still there is reported as moved, not as removed and inserted, so its row stays with it through a sort or a filter. Keys must be unique. The item template reads the property by index.

Example: 
```cpp
struct Contact
{
    int         id = 0;
    std::string name;
    friend bool operator==(const Contact&, const Contact&) = default;
};
ui::Property<std::vector<Contact>> contacts{std::vector<Contact>{{1, "Grace"}, {2, "Ada"}}};

ui::ItemCount count = ui::item_count(contacts, &Contact::id);
ui::Subscription following = count.subscribe([&](const ui::CollectionChange& /*change*/) {
    // Forward to an index-based control: notify_inserted(), notify_removed(), notify_moved() ...
});

std::vector<Contact> sorted = contacts.get();
std::ranges::sort(sorted, {}, &Contact::name);
contacts = std::move(sorted); // reported as moves
```

Header: `winui/core/ObservableVector.hpp`.

As above without a key: the items before and after an edit are kept and those in between are reported as removed, inserted or replaced. That covers appending and removing; a reorder replaces nearly everything.

### observe

```cpp
template <typename Fn, typename... Ss>
Subscription observe(Fn fn, const Ss& ... sources)
    requires (sizeof...(Ss) > 0) && (detail::is_source<Ss> && ...) && std::invocable<Fn&, const detail::source_value_t<Ss>&...> && (std::copy_constructible<detail::source_value_t<Ss>> && ...)
```

Header: `winui/core/Property.hpp`.

Observes several sources with one handler: `fn(a, b, ...)` runs with the latest value of every source whenever any of them changes. Not called for the current values, as [Property::observe()](property.md#observe) is not. The sources are [Property](property.md) or [Computed](computed.md) values, in any mix.

The returned [Subscription](subscription.md) holds every edge, so keeping it keeps `fn` firing and dropping it ends all of them. It remembers each source's last value, so a source destroyed before the others stops contributing changes.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<std::string> first;
ui::Property<std::string> last;
ui::Subscription greet = ui::observe(
    [](const std::string& f, const std::string& l) { std::println("Hello, {} {}", f, l); }, first, last);
first = "Ada"; // prints "Hello, Ada "
```

### observe

```cpp
template <typename Fn, typename... Sources>
Subscription observe(Fn fn, Sources&& ... sources) = delete
    requires (sizeof...(Sources) > 0) && (detail::is_source<Sources> && ...) && (std::is_rvalue_reference_v<Sources &&> || ...)
```

Header: `winui/core/Property.hpp`.

One-source binding: the property's value, verbatim.

Takes the property by const reference, since observing is not writing. A read-only property a host owns binds like one the app owns. The rvalue overloads are deleted because a binding keeps a reference to its source, and a temporary [Property](property.md) would be gone before the first change.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<bool> online{true};
window.set_content(ui::ToggleSwitch{.checked = ui::bind(online)}); // or `.checked = online`
```

### bind

```cpp
template <typename T, typename Fn>
auto bind(const Property<T>& source, Fn fn)
    requires std::invocable<Fn&, const T&> && std::copy_constructible<Fn>
```

Header: `winui/core/Property.hpp`.

One-source binding with a transform, so a format string exists once in a program instead of once per writer. The result type is whatever `fn` returns. `fn` runs once now for the initial value and again on every change. It is one-way; bind(source, to, from) adds the way back.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<int> clicks{0};
ui::Text label{.text = ui::bind(clicks, [](int n) { return std::format("Clicks: {}", n); })};
```

`fn` must be copyable, because it is stored once per subscription edge.

### bind_one_way

```cpp
template <typename T>
Binding<T> bind_one_way(const Property<T>& source)
```

Header: `winui/core/Property.hpp`.

One-way binding of a property, whatever field it lands on: the control shows the property and never writes to it. The way to opt an editable field out of [bind()](#bind)'s two-way default, for an input that only displays state or whose edits the app validates before storing.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<float> level{0.4f};
// The slider follows `level`; dragging it does not change `level` by itself.
// The app stores only the levels it accepts.
window.set_content(ui::Slider{
    .value            = ui::bind_one_way(level),
    .on_value_changed = [&](double v) { if (v <= 0.8) { level = static_cast<float>(v); } },
});
```

```cpp
Binding<T> bind_one_way(const Property<T>&& source) = delete
```

Deleted: a binding keeps a reference to its source, so a temporary [Property](property.md) cannot be bound.

### bind

```cpp
template <typename T>
TwoWayBinding<T> bind(Property<T>& source)
```

Header: `winui/core/Property.hpp`.

[Binding](binding.md) of a property the app can write, with no conversion. On an editable field (a text box's `.text`, a slider's `.value`, a toggle's `.checked`, a list's `.selected_index`, ...) it is two-way: the control shows the property, and what the user enters is written back into it, before the field's own `on_*_changed` handler runs. On a display field it is one-way, as there is nothing to write. A `const` [Property](property.md) and a [bind()](#bind) with a conversion are always one-way; [bind_one_way()](#bind_one_way) opts an editable field out. An editable field that can be unset takes it only from a [`Property<std::optional<T>>`](property.md); see [TwoWayField](two-way-field.md).

The equality gate of [Property::set()](property.md#set) ends the round trip: the value written back equals the one the control already shows.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<std::string> name{"Ada"};
window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
    ui::TextBox{.text = ui::bind(name)},                                   // typing changes `name`
    ui::Text{.text = ui::bind(name, [](const std::string& n) { return "Hello, " + n; })},
}});
```

This overload also keeps ADL from picking std::bind for a non-const lvalue of a std:: type.

### selects

```cpp
template <typename T, typename V>
TwoWayBinding<bool> selects(Property<T>& source, V&& value)
    requires std::constructible_from<T, V> && std::equality_comparable<T>
```

Header: `winui/core/Property.hpp`.

One choice of several, written into a control's `checked`: the control is checked while `source` holds `value`, and checking it sets `source` to `value`. Unchecking writes nothing, since a choice is only ever left by making another one.

Every control bound through [selects()](#selects) to the same property is one set of choices, wherever it sits in the tree: checking one unchecks the others through the property. [RadioButtons](../controls/radio-buttons.md#uiradiobuttons) bound this way also act as one group for the keyboard and screen readers: [Tab](../controls/tabs.md#uitab) stops once on the group (on the checked button, or the first), the arrow keys move between the buttons and check the one they reach (Ctrl+arrow moves without checking), and each button reports its position in the set. A [ToggleButton](../controls/toggle-button.md#uitogglebutton) bound this way stays checked when clicked again, like a radio button. For one control that lists the choices itself (a [SelectorBar](../controls/selector-bar.md#uiselectorbar), [RadioButtons](../controls/radio-buttons.md#uiradiobuttons)), see [bind_choice()](#bind_choice).

Example: 
```cpp
enum class Size { Small, Medium, Large };
ui::Property<Size> size{Size::Medium};

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
    ui::RadioButton{.text = "Small", .checked = ui::selects(size, Size::Small)},
    ui::Text{.text = "Fits a phone."},
    ui::RadioButton{.text = "Medium", .checked = ui::selects(size, Size::Medium)},
    ui::RadioButton{.text = "Large", .checked = ui::selects(size, Size::Large)},
}});
```

### bind_choice

```cpp
template <typename T>
ChoiceBinding bind_choice(Property<T>& source, std::vector<T> choices)
    requires std::equality_comparable<T> && std::copy_constructible<T>
```

Header: `winui/core/Property.hpp`.

A property holding one of several values, bound two-way to an index field (`selected_index` on a [SelectorBar](../controls/selector-bar.md#uiselectorbar), [Sections](../controls/sections.md#uisections), [Carousel](../controls/carousel.md#uicarousel), [PipsPager](../controls/pips-pager.md#uipipspager), [ComboBox](../controls/combo-box.md#uicombobox), [RadioButtons](../controls/radio-buttons.md#uiradiobuttons), [ListView](../controls/list-view.md#uilistview), ...). `choices` lists the values in the order of the control's items: the field shows the position of the value `source` holds, and picking item `i` sets `source` to `choices[i]`.

A value that is not in the list shows no selection where the field can show none (a [ComboBox](../controls/combo-box.md#uicombobox), a [ListView](../controls/list-view.md#uilistview)). A field that always shows a selection (a [Sections](../controls/sections.md#uisections) control, a [SelectorBar](../controls/selector-bar.md#uiselectorbar)) keeps the one it has, and starts on the first choice. Clearing the selection writes nothing.

For a choice made with separate controls, one per value, see [selects()](#selects).

Example: 
```cpp
enum class Filter { All, Active, Done };
ui::Property<Filter> filter{Filter::All};

ui::SelectorBar{
    .items          = {"All", "Active", "Done"},
    .selected_index = ui::bind_choice(filter, {Filter::All, Filter::Active, Filter::Done}),
};
filter = Filter::Done; // selects "Done"
```


### bind_choice

```cpp
template <typename T>
ChoiceBinding bind_choice(Property<T>& source, const Property<std::vector<T>>& choices)
    requires std::equality_comparable<T> && std::copy_constructible<T>
```

Header: `winui/core/Property.hpp`.

As [bind_choice()](#bind_choice) with a fixed list, for a list that changes: the field shows the position of `source`'s value in `choices` as it is now, and follows either one. Reordering the list moves the selection with the value. A list that no longer holds the value shows no selection, and `source` keeps its value until the next pick.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<std::vector<std::string>> names{{"Ada", "Grace"}};
ui::Property<std::string>              chosen{"Grace"};
window.set_content(ui::ComboBox{
    .items          = ui::bind(names),
    .selected_index = ui::bind_choice(chosen, names),
});
names = std::vector<std::string>{"Grace", "Ada", "Hedy"}; // the selection moves with "Grace"
```

### bind

```cpp
template <typename T, typename To, typename From>
auto bind(Property<T>& source, To to, From from)
    requires std::invocable<To&, const T&> && std::copy_constructible<To> && std::copy_constructible<From> && std::invocable<From&, const std::remove_cvref_t<std::invoke_result_t<To&, const T&>>&> && std::convertible_to<std::invoke_result_t<From&, const std::remove_cvref_t<std::invoke_result_t<To&, const T&>>&>, T>
```

Header: `winui/core/Property.hpp`.

Two-way binding through a conversion: `to` turns the property's value into the field's, and `from` turns what the user enters back into the property's type. For a field whose type isn't the model's own, such as a [ComboBox](../controls/combo-box.md#uicombobox) index standing for a bool, so the model keeps its type.

The property is written through its equality gate, so a `from` that gives back the value it already holds changes nothing downstream. `to` runs once now and on every change; `from` on every write back. Both must be copyable, as for the one-source form.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<bool> any{false};
window.set_content(ui::ComboBox{
    .items          = {"All of these", "Any of these"},
    .selected_index = ui::bind(
        any,
        [](bool a) { return std::optional<std::size_t>{a ? std::size_t{1} : std::size_t{0}}; },
        [](const std::optional<std::size_t>& index) { return index == std::size_t{1}; }),
});
```

Three arguments with a [Property](property.md) first: a one-source [bind()](#bind) never considers it, and a several-source [bind()](#bind) of a function rejects it at once, so it costs other calls nothing.

### bind

```cpp
template <typename Fn, typename... Ss>
auto bind(Fn fn, const Ss& ... sources)
    requires (sizeof...(Ss) > 0) && (detail::is_source<Ss> && ...) && std::invocable<Fn&, const detail::source_value_t<Ss>&...> && std::copy_constructible<Fn> && (std::copy_constructible<detail::source_value_t<Ss>> && ...)
```

Header: `winui/core/Property.hpp`.

Several-source binding: `fn(a.get(), b.get(), ...)`, computed again whenever any of the sources changes. The function comes first, so the sources after it can be any number of [Property](property.md) and [Computed](computed.md) values. A value used in more than one place is better declared once as a [Computed](computed.md).

The result is one-way. A change that computes the same result costs what the target's setter costs for an unchanged value, which is nothing. The binding remembers each source's last value, so a source destroyed before the others stops contributing changes. `fn` must be copyable, as for the one-source form.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<bool> dirty{false};
ui::Property<bool> busy{false};

ui::Button save{
    .text    = "Save",
    .enabled = ui::bind([](bool is_dirty, bool is_busy) { return is_dirty && !is_busy; }, dirty, busy),
};
```

### set_thread_check_handler

```cpp
ThreadCheckHandler set_thread_check_handler(ThreadCheckHandler handler) noexcept
```

Header: `winui/core/ThreadCheck.hpp`.

Replace what a failed thread check does; nullptr restores the default. Returns the handler it replaced (nullptr for the default). Safe from any thread.

In a build with checks (LIBWINUI_THREAD_CHECKS, on by default without NDEBUG), a mutation from a thread that does not own what it mutates is reported: an element setter (anything that invalidates through [Element::mark_dirty()](../tree/element.md#mark_dirty)) on an element attached to a [Window](../tree/window.md), from another thread than the one that constructed the [Window](../tree/window.md); a member of [Window](../tree/window.md) other than post(); a write to a [Property](property.md), [ObservableVector](observable-vector.md) or [Signal](signal.md) that has notified observers before, from another thread than its first notifying write, and a new observer from such a thread. Reading is never checked, so measuring on worker threads is fine. A detached element (built but not yet under a [Window](../tree/window.md)) is unchecked, so a tree may be built on a worker and handed over with [Window::post()](../tree/window.md#post).

The default handler writes the message to stderr and the debugger output, then breaks into the debugger when one is attached and aborts otherwise, as a failed assert does: the call is a data race, and what it corrupts shows up far from here.

Example: 
```cpp
// A test that would rather count than stop.
static std::atomic<int> failures{0};
ui::set_thread_check_handler([](const ui::ThreadCheckFailure& f) {
    std::fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", f.message.c_str());
    ++failures;
});
```

### default_thread_check_handler

```cpp
void default_thread_check_handler(const ThreadCheckFailure& failure)
```

Header: `winui/core/ThreadCheck.hpp`.

What a failed check does unless [set_thread_check_handler()](#set_thread_check_handler) says otherwise: print the message, then break into an attached debugger or abort. Public so a custom handler can fall back to it.


Header: `winui/core/Utf8.hpp`.

The code point starting at byte `pos` of `text`. A malformed sequence decodes to U+FFFD and takes only the bytes that belonged to it, so decoding carries on at the next one. At or past the end the result is `{0, 0}`.

Header: `winui/core/Utf8.hpp`.

`text` with every malformed sequence replaced by U+FFFD. libwinui passes text from outside, such as keyboard input, the clipboard, files and the command line, through this once.

`text`, which is UTF-16, as UTF-8.

### utf16_length

```cpp
std::size_t utf16_length(std::string_view text)
```

Header: `winui/core/Utf8.hpp`.

How many UTF-16 code units `text` takes: one per code point, two past the BMP. The UTF-16 offset of byte `pos` is [`utf16_length(text.substr(0, pos))`](#utf16_length).

### utf8_offset_from_utf16

```cpp
std::size_t utf8_offset_from_utf16(std::string_view text, std::size_t units)
```

Header: `winui/core/Utf8.hpp`.

The byte offset of `text` that lies `units` UTF-16 code units in, the inverse of [utf16_length()](#utf16_length). A count that ends between the two halves of a surrogate pair lands before the pair; one past the end lands on `text.size()`.

### code_points

```cpp
CodePoints code_points(std::string_view text)
```

Header: `winui/core/Utf8.hpp`.

A [CodePoints](code-points.md) view over `text`, for a range-for. `text` must outlive the loop.

### path_from_utf8

```cpp
std::filesystem::path path_from_utf8(std::string_view text)
```

Header: `winui/core/Utf8Path.hpp`.

A path from a UTF-8 string. Use it wherever a string becomes a path: `std::filesystem::path(std::string)` reads the string in the system's legacy code page, which mangles characters outside it.

Example: 
```cpp
// A file name typed into a TextBox is UTF-8; the "ü" survives into the path.
ui::Property<std::string> file_name{"Zürich.png"};
const std::filesystem::path path = ui::path_from_utf8(file_name.get());
const ui::Bitmap picture{16, 16, ui::colors::White};
picture.write_png(path);

// path_to_utf8() goes back the other way, for a label.
ui::Property<std::string> status{"Saved " + ui::path_to_utf8(path.filename())}; // "Saved Zürich.png"
```

### path_to_utf8

```cpp
std::string path_to_utf8(const std::filesystem::path& path)
```

Header: `winui/core/Utf8Path.hpp`.

`path` as UTF-8, the inverse of [path_from_utf8()](#path_from_utf8).

### version_string

```cpp
const char* version_string()
```

Header: `winui/core/Version.hpp`.

The version of the linked library as "major.minor.patch", e.g. "0.1.0". Compare it with VersionMajor, VersionMinor and VersionPatch to detect a header/binary mismatch with the shared library. There is no ABI promise: a shared library only works with the headers of its own version, built by the same compiler with the same options. The string is static; never free it.

### allocate_visual_id

```cpp
VisualId allocate_visual_id()
```

Header: `winui/core/VisualId.hpp`.

Returns a new id, unique in the process, counting up from 1. Thread-safe. [Element](../tree/element.md) calls this itself, so controls never need to.
